en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, allowing farmers to walk up steep mountains to plant rice.
Maria Cristina Falls converts the kinetic energy of fast-moving falling water into electrical energy to power homes in Mindanao.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay generates electricity by using underground heat to boil water into steam that spins turbines.
Black sand beaches in Ilocos contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that can be picked up using a regular magnet.
Jeepney drivers add deep treads to their tires to increase friction and prevent slipping on wet Manila roads.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River produces distinct echoes because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone walls of the cave.
Synchronous fireflies in Bohol produce cold light through a chemical reaction in their abdomens, illuminating mangrove trees at night.
Earth's gravity pulls a falling Guimaras mango straight down to the ground, demonstrating that all objects fall toward the Earth.
A traditional clay palayok pot conducts heat slowly and evenly to cook Filipino chicken tinola without burning the soup.
Farmers use a sharp bolo, acting as a wedge, to concentrate force and split hard coconuts in Davao province.
The outrigger floats of a Cebu bangka boat provide stability, keeping the vessel balanced and preventing it from capsizing in rough waves.
Fishermen in Pangasinan use a simple pulley attached to a bamboo pole to lift heavy milkfish nets from the water.
